sources_considered.why: The speaker's own post. Read only to understand where the $250 billion figure comes from (his $500 billion hypothetical and 190GW buildout estimate), not as evidence.

receipt.public_excerpt: It said it was committed to spending on Amazon's Trainium chips at $110 billion through 2036, and $114.5 billion on Google TPUs through 2033.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows the scale of one lab's multi-year compute commitments. These are spread over a decade, so they do not test how much extra annual demand from other companies is needed to justify the buildout.

unresolved_gaps: No agreed standard exists for how much annual compute revenue would 'justify' the planned data-center buildout. The answer depends on the model and the assumptions used.
The $250 billion figure is measured against a $500 billion-a-year OpenAI-plus-Anthropic spending level that the speaker himself sets up, not against a reported baseline.
No deadline is given, so no future observation would clearly settle whether the requirement was right.
